mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of fractions are equivalent rational representations?
mcqs.explanation: 14 ÷ 21 = 2 ÷ 3 = 2/3, so the two fractions represent the same rational number. The other pairs simplify to different values (9/12 = 3/4 ≠ 5/7, 8/16 = 1/2 ≠ 1/3, 5/15 = 1/3 ≠ 2/5). Hence only option A shows equivalent rational representations.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify rational numbers in everyday contexts
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday quantities is a rational number?

options.A: The exact length of a diagonal of a square with side 1 cm (√2 cm)
options.B: The price of an item listed as $1.25
options.D: The circumference of a circle with radius 1 m expressed as 2π m

mcqs.answer: The price of an item listed as $1.25
mcqs.explanation: A rational number can be written as a quotient of two integers. $1.25 = 125/100 = 5/4, so it is rational. √2, π, and 2π are known to be irrational because they cannot be expressed as a fraction of integers.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand rational numbers as numbers expressible as a quotient of integers with non-zero denominator
mcqs.question: Which statement best defines a rational number?

options.A: A number that can be expressed as a quotient of two integers with a non‑zero denominator
options.B: A number that cannot be written as a fraction
options.C: A number that is only positive
options.D: A number that has a terminating decimal representation only

mcqs.answer: A number that can be expressed as a quotient of two integers with a non‑zero denominator
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a rational number is any number that can be written in the form p/q where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. Options B, C, and D describe properties that are not required for rationality (irrational numbers cannot be written as fractions, rational numbers can be negative, and some rational numbers have repeating, not just terminating, decimals).

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise positive and negative rational numbers
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is true about the rational numbers –3/4 and 5/6?
mcqs.explanation: A rational number is negative when its numerator and denominator have opposite signs. –3/4 has a negative numerator, so it is negative. 5/6 has both numerator and denominator positive, so it is positive. Hence option C correctly describes their signs.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent rational numbers on a number line
mcqs.question: On a number line, which point correctly represents the rational number –2/3?

options.A: A point two units to the right of zero
options.B: A point two thirds to the left of zero
options.C: A point three halves to the right of zero
options.D: A point one half to the left of zero

mcqs.answer: A point two thirds to the left of zero
mcqs.explanation: Negative rational numbers lie to the left of zero. –2/3 is located two thirds of a unit left of the origin. Options A and C are to the right of zero, and D represents –1/2, not –2/3.

mcqs.question: Which of the following rational numbers is the greatest?
mcqs.explanation: Convert to decimals: 3/5 = 0.60, 7/10 = 0.70, 2/3 ≈ 0.666…, 5/8 = 0.625. The largest value is 0.70, which corresponds to 7/10. Therefore option B is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an equivalent form of the fraction 9/12?
mcqs.explanation: Dividing numerator and denominator of 9/12 by their greatest common divisor 3 gives 9÷3 = 3 and 12÷3 = 4, so 9/12 = 3/4. The other options simplify to different values.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify rational numbers in everyday contexts
mcqs.question: A student records the following measurements: (i) The length of a hallway is 12.5 m. (ii) The value of √5 m. (iii) The time taken to run 400 m is 58.2 s. (iv) The number π approximated as 3.14159. Which of these quantities are rational numbers?
mcqs.explanation: 12.5 = 25/2 and 58.2 = 582/10 are both fractions of integers, so they are rational. √5 and π are known irrational numbers because they cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers. Hence only (i) and (iii) are rational.
